title: Cancellation during ledger I/O can still return an SDK allow

significance.impact: A callback can return an allow after cancellation arrived during its read or release operation.
significance.exposure: Uncommitted callback below a closed production gate. Deterministic planted-ledger cases reproduce both windows; no native action was executed.
significance.detectability: Cancellation tests that signal only during polling miss both synchronous-I/O windows.
significance.systemic_implication: The callback must recheck observed cancellation at consequential I/O boundaries; shared transport admission remains an independent guard.
significance.recovery: Repair the callback and preserve already committed one-use releases as consumed; never infer delivery or replay authority.
significance.rationale: A material callback lifecycle error, contained by the shared transport cancellation event and disabled production route. No native execution bypass is established.

confidence.basis: Independent source discovery followed by two intended pre-repair assertion failures.

evidence.observation: Both inspect and take_decision cases failed because CancelledError was not raised after the planted cancellation signal.

claim.failure_mode: The callback checks a thread event before synchronous ledger I/O, then releases and returns without observing cancellation that arrived during that I/O.
claim.downstream_consequence: The callback can emit a misleading allow and consume a decision unnecessarily; a correctly shared transport event still prevents native input admission.

counterevidence.observation: The transport independently checks the same cancellation event before accepting a response.

proof_limits: A release can legitimately win a concurrent ledger-close transaction; these checks do not provide atomic ordering against every subsequent side effect.
No native delivery, tool action, or installed approval-route claim.

containment: Production on-request is disabled; the shared process cancellation signal independently prevents transport admission.

remediation.description: Recheck cancellation after the read snapshot and after recording a committed release as consumed, before returning any SDK decision.

evidence.observation: Post-snapshot cancellation withdraws unreleased authority; post-release cancellation preserves the consumed record without emitting a response.

performed.independence_basis: The separate source reviewer identified the failure and re-examined the repair. Parent-executed planted interleavings and actual SDK control dispatch supplied distinct behavioral observations.

evidence.observation: Both boundary regressions pass after their intended pre-fix failures; the post-mutation callback/ledger/transport suite passed all 62 cases. Independent re-review found no remaining callback-local source defect.

performed.negative_control: Signals planted during inspect and take_decision caused the original source to fail at DID NOT RAISE CancelledError. The repaired tests also distinguish an unreleased withdrawal from an already committed, non-replayable release.
